transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Patel (CISO, Northstar), Mark Reynolds (VP Eng), Aisha Khan (Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private options, SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, and data residency. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, schedule deep technical session for private deployment, run a pilot for dedicated capacity.

Topics: Security certifications, access controls, encryption, key management, audit logging, retention/purge policy, private deployment network requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro, then Daniel will cover the architecture and we can go through your security questions.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks. Yeah, key thing for us is understanding what level of compliance Redwood has — SOC 2, any ISO, and then we need details on how long you retain PII from calls and logs.
[00:30] Daniel: Absolutely. High level first: Redwood operates Hosted, Dedicated and Private — hosted is our multi-tenant public API, dedicated is reserved GPU pools for a single tenant, and private is customer-managed VPC or on-prem. Each has different controls for isolation and key mgmt.
[01:05] Mark: Quick question — do you have SOC 2 Type II? And ISO 27001?
[01:12] Sofia: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II. We're in the process of maintaining ISO 27001 — we have the summary artifacts, will share ISO gap notes. We'll send the full SOC 2 report under an NDA.
[01:30] Aisha: Great. About SSO — we use SAML with SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. Can we integrate?
[01:40] Daniel: Yes — we support SAML and OIDC for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For Hosted customers we provide SAML SSO and SCIM; for Dedicated and Private, you can enable SSO against your IdP and control user provisioning into the console. There might be small diffs in attribute mapping, we can share mappings.
[02:05] Priya: How about RBAC? Our security policy requires role separation and fine-grained permissions.
[02:13] Daniel: We have role-based access controls with built-in roles (Admin, Operator, Reader) and you can create custom roles. For Dedicated/Private you can map to groups from your IdP and we log role changes in the audit trail.
[02:30] Mark: On audit logs — what's retained and can logs be pushed to our SIEM?
[02:36] Sofia: We retain operational audit logs for a default of 90 days in Hosted but we can extend retention for enterprise customers. We provide audit export integrations — syslog/S3/Cloud Storage and streaming to SIEMs via log forwarders for Dedicated and Private.
[03:00] Priya: And those logs include prompts and model inputs?
[03:04] Daniel: Prompt-level logging is configurable. By default Hosted keeps minimal logs for debugging and abuse detection — we redact PII on ingestion where possible. For customers that require zero retention of inputs, Private deployment or Dedicated with data purge policies is recommended.
[03:28] Aisha: Do you offer customer-managed keys? We require CMEK for some workloads.
[03:33] Daniel: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMEK) for encryption at rest — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault supported depending on deployment. For Private deployments you can bring your own key material and control rotation. For Hosted we can offer CMEK under enterprise contracts; will need scope in the agreement.
[03:58] Mark: What's encrypted in transit vs at rest?
[04:01] Sofia: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. At rest we encrypt S3/Blob storage and databases, and disk encryption on nodes. Keys are handled by a KMS, either Redwood-managed or customer-managed.
[04:20] Priya: We also need to know about data residency — we process patient-adjacent data, so EU residency matters for some customers.
[04:28] Daniel: We have regional deployments and ability to pin workloads to regions. Hosted can be region-restricted; Dedicated and Private give more control — Private gives you the most control since it runs in your VPC/region. We'll need to capture your retention and residency requirements in the questionnaire.
[04:50] Aisha: About legal hold/forensics — if we need to preserve data for an investigation, is there support?
[04:56] Daniel: Yes, we can support legal hold in Dedicated and Private; Hosted requires a discussion but we can extend retention and provide export. We also offer immutable audit snapshots for compliance reviews under enterprise packages.
[05:18] Priya: Are you able to provide pen test results and vulnerability scans?
[05:22] Sofia: We can provide redacted pentest summaries and scan reports. We'll include the latest ones in the compliance pack.
[05:30] Mark: On network controls — for Private, do you support private endpoints and no public ingress?
[05:36] Daniel: Private supports air-gapped on-prem installs or VPC deployments with private endpoints. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering or private links depending on cloud. We also support static allowlists for API egress.
[05:54] Aisha: How about secrets management inside the runtime — do you ever surface customer secrets in logs?
[05:59] Daniel: We have strong controls to avoid logging secrets. We do input redaction heuristics, and you can configure stricter sanitization rules. For highest assurance we recommend Private where you control the entire runtime and KMS.
[06:20] Priya: Regarding model artifacts — where are model weights stored and who can access them?
[06:27] Daniel: Model weights for open models are stored on encrypted blob storage. Access is limited to the runtime and orchestrator nodes; we currently don't exfiltrate weights. If you run Private, weights remain within your environment.
[06:45] Mark: Do you provide attestations for data deletion? We need proof of purge for some regs.
[06:50] Sofia: Yes — we can provide deletion attestations and logs showing wipe operations for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we provide logs of purge events and can coordinate with you on retention windows.
[07:05] Priya: Who has access to production environments at Redwood?
[07:10] Daniel: Access is limited to authorized SREs and a small set of engineers under least privilege, with just-in-time access and session recording for escalations. Access events are logged and audited.
[07:30] Aisha: Do you have incident response playbooks and notification SLAs?
[07:35] Sofia: Yes — incident response runbooks, communication templates, and security on-call rotation. For enterprise deals we can agree to notification SLAs. We'll include an incident playbook excerpt in the packet.
[07:55] Mark: For the Dedicated pilot we want to test latency and a full security review. Can we get a short-term Dedicated environment with encrypted volumes + CMEK?
[08:05] Daniel: Yes — we can provision a pilot Dedicated cluster with CMEK and VPC peering. We'll scope network egress, sample size for load tests, and a timeframe — typically 2–4 weeks for pilot provisioning depending on region and capacity.
[08:30] Priya: Any concerns about model hallucinations or PII leakage from generated outputs?
[08:36] Daniel: We recommend prompt engineering and output filters; Redwood also supports response steering and safety layers. For regulated data we suggest not using hosted unless inputs are transient and fully redacted, or else use Private.
[08:55] Sofia: Quick note — some transcripts auto-replace product names, so apologies if you see Redwood product names spelled weird in the notes.
[09:02] (laughter)
[09:10] Aisha: How does billing and data access intersect — do you retain request logs for billing reconciliation?
[09:16] Sofia: Billing logs are retained for 12 months by default; we can export usage detail to your billing system. Usage logs can be separated from input logs to limit exposure.
[09:36] Mark: Any SOC2 controls around change management and patching cadence?
[09:41] Daniel: We follow documented change management with scheduled patch windows, emergency patch procedures, and we record change tickets and approvals — those are part of the SOC 2 controls.
[09:58] Priya: What's your default data retention for request payloads in Hosted?
[10:03] Daniel: Hosted default is 30 days for request payloads used for debugging and abuse detection; we mask PII when detected. We can shorten that with contractual terms, or you can choose Dedicated/Private if you require no retention.
[10:24] Aisha: For the security questionnaire, what level of detail will you provide?
[10:29] Sofia: We'll provide an answered questionnaire, SOC2 report (redacted), the most recent pentest summary, and architecture diagrams. We'll also include a short doc on SSO and SCIM attribute mappings.
[10:45] Mark: Do you have MFA enforced for Redwood Console access?
[10:49] Daniel: Yes — MFA is required for all accounts; for Hosted customers we also support enforcing MFA via SAML IdP policies.
[10:58] Priya: Are you able to sign a data processing agreement and any BAA if needed?
[11:04] Sofia: We can sign a DPA and we have a standard BAA template for healthcare customers; we'll route that through legal once we have preliminary requirements.
[11:20] (short pause)
[11:25] Mark: What about monitoring and tracing on the runtime — can we get request-level traces?
[11:31] Daniel: We emit traces and metrics; you can integrate with OpenTelemetry and we can provide traces for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can provide aggregate traces and select request-level traces under enterprise packages.
[11:52] Aisha: If we decide on Private, what does the install footprint look like?
[11:56] Daniel: For VPC Private it's a few nodes for the control plane and GPU workers depending on throughput. For on-prem it's an appliance model — we'll send an install sizing doc.
[12:10] Priya: Are there any known compliance blockers for us as a health-adjacent org?
[12:16] Sofia: Not specifically; the main blockers are data residency and whether you need BAA-level handling of PHI. We generally recommend Private or Dedicated with strict retention for PHI-like data.
[12:34] Mark: Can we get a demo of the audit log UI and role mapping next week?
[12:38] Sofia: Absolutely, we can demo the console and logs — Daniel can walk through role creation and SCIM mapping.
[12:47] Daniel: I'll prepare a demo with example audit streams and SIEM export.
[12:52] Priya: One last thing — can you confirm deletion windows and attestations again? We need proof for regulators.
[12:59] Sofia: Yes — deletion attestations and logs are available for Dedicated/Private; Hosted we can provide evidence of purge events, though attestations for Hosted depend on contract terms.
[13:15] Mark: Sounds good. We'll fill out the questionnaire and get back with timelines.
[13:20] Sofia: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the compliance pack and schedule the deep dive.
